newsitem.title: CHINA: China says wants farmers to help store grain.
newsitem.headline: China says wants farmers to help store grain.

text.p: Chinese Vice Premier Zhu Rongji has called on farmers to help store grain as government stockpiles rise, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
Zhu, the nation's top official for economic policy, told an agricultural conference that the state would protect the interests of farmers by buying grain at guaranteed prices.
But he also told the conference that ended on Friday that it was difficult for the state to store much more grain, the news agency said.

Zhu had said earlier last week that grain reserves stood at an all-time high. He did not give a figure for reserves but China has reported a bumper summer harvest for the third consecutive year, resulting in a drop in grain prices in some places.
Officials have forecast China's summer grain harvest at from 115 million tonnes to 118 million tonnes, up from 111 million last year.
The Ministry of Internal Trade has forecast grain output for this year at above 484 million tonnes, compared with a record 490 million tonnes last year.
In some areas, local authorities have this year been buying grain intended to fulfil government quotas at market prices, which are currently lower than the state prices, officials have said.
